```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Primary analysis on all assessments, and a sensitivity analysis with one
assessment per organisation (the first), because some organisations completed
the assessment more than once.

# Package versions

The analysis is run with the package versions reported in the manuscript
(psych 2.5.3 and lavaan 0.6-19). They are installed once into a separate folder,
so the normal R library is not changed. Set `use_manuscript_versions <- FALSE`
to run the analysis with the currently installed versions instead.

```{r install_manuscript_versions, eval=FALSE}
# Run this chunk ONCE by hand (it is skipped when knitting).
lib_orig <- "../r_lib_manuscript_versions"
dir.create(lib_orig, showWarnings = FALSE)

install.packages("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/psych/psych_2.5.3.tar.gz",
                 repos = NULL, type = "source", lib = lib_orig)
install.packages("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/lavaan/lavaan_0.6-19.tar.gz",
                 repos = NULL, type = "source", lib = lib_orig)

packageVersion("lavaan", lib.loc = "../r_lib_manuscript_versions")   # should say 0.6.19
```

```{r packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
use_manuscript_versions <- TRUE
lib_orig <- "../r_lib_manuscript_versions"

if (use_manuscript_versions) {
  if (!dir.exists(lib_orig)) {
    stop("Folder '", lib_orig, "' not found. Run the chunk 'install_manuscript_versions' once first.")
  }
  # Look in the folder with the manuscript versions first
  .libPaths(c(normalizePath(lib_orig), .libPaths()))
}

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)        # EFA
library(lavaan)       # CFA
library(GPArotation)  # oblimin rotation
library(ggplot2)

# Stop if the wrong versions are loaded (restart R and run again if this fails)
if (use_manuscript_versions) {
  stopifnot(packageVersion("psych")  == "2.5.3",
            packageVersion("lavaan") == "0.6-19")
}
cat("R:", as.character(getRversion()),
    "| psych:", as.character(packageVersion("psych")),
    "| lavaan:", as.character(packageVersion("lavaan")),
    "| GPArotation:", as.character(packageVersion("GPArotation")), "\n")
```

# Settings

```{r settings}
file       <- "./data/Ruwe resultaten 2022 tot met dec 2024 sdw gecombineerd.xlsx"
org_id_col <- "Respondent id"   # column that identifies the organisation
time_col   <- "Jaar"   # column with the assessment year or date

n_factors <- 7        # number of factors in the EFA
cutoff    <- 0.32     # items with all |loadings| below this are removed
seed      <- 20261007 # for the parallel analysis
out_dir   <- "./results/sensitivity_repeated_assessments"
```

# 2. Repeated assessments

```{r repeated_assessments}
stopifnot(!is.null(org_id_col), !is.null(time_col))

org_id <- trimws(do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(df_raw[org_id_col])), sep = " | ")))
assessment_time <- df_raw[[time_col]]

cat("Assessments:", nrow(df_raw), "\nUnique organisations:", length(unique(org_id)), "\n")
print(table(assessments_per_organisation = table(org_id)))

# First assessment of each organisation (ties are broken by the order in the file)
chron <- order(assessment_time, seq_len(nrow(df_raw)))
first_rows <- sort(chron[!duplicated(org_id[chron])])

dat_all  <- dvc_items                              # primary sample
dat_sens <- dvc_items[first_rows, , drop = FALSE]  # sensitivity sample

# Assessments per year in both samples
year <- if (inherits(assessment_time, c("Date", "POSIXt"))) format(assessment_time, "%Y") else
  sub(".*?(20[0-9]{2}).*", "\\1", as.character(assessment_time), perl = TRUE)
print(rbind(all_assessments = table(year), sensitivity_sample = table(factor(year[first_rows], levels = sort(unique(year))))))
```

# 3. Confirmatory factor analysis

Thresholds: CFI $\geq 0.95$, RMSEA $\leq 0.06$, SRMR $\leq 0.08$. The estimator is
WLSMV, so the scaled CFI and RMSEA are the ones to report.

```{r cfa}
model <- '
  # LD: Leadership and data-culture
  LD =~ ld01_data_awareness + ld02_finance_ownership + ld03_leadership_curiosity +
        ld04_dgw_planning_theme + ld05_dgw_dev_budget + ld06_data_project_based +
        ld07_data_initiation + ld08_dgw_strategic_theme + ld09_data_strategy +
        ld10_cdo_present + ld11_dgw_struct_budget + ld12_data_value_proven +
        ld13_bi_entity + ld14_data_driven_norm

  # SG: Strategy & Governance
  SG =~ sg15_qualitative_goals + sg16_financial_reporting + sg17_ad_hoc_reactive +
        sg18_quantified_goals + sg19_financial_orientation + sg20_bi_translation +
        sg21_interdisciplinary_prioritization + sg22_goal_adjustment +
        sg23_data_driven_goals + sg24_partner_datascience_collab

  # PW: Process oriented work
  PW =~ pw25_data_process_documented + pw26_workflow_translation +
        pw27_methodical_datapilots + pw28_privacy_officer_involved +
        pw29_dgw_protocols + pw30_data_in_policy + pw31_steering_info_access +
        pw32_data_in_innovation + pw33_ethical_data_processing + pw34_data_driven_redesign

  # DQ: Definitions and data quality
  DQ =~ dq35_fixed_definitions + dq36_coordination_definitions +
        dq37_org_wide_data_agreements + dq38_data_reliability +
        dq39_practical_definitions + dq40_info_understandable +
        dq41_data_mgmt_and_analytics + dq42_external_data_enrichment +
        dq43_data_for_prediction + dq44_data_for_ml_dev + dq45_controlled_dataflows

  # AT: Architecture and tools
  AT =~ at46_app_data_collection + at47_external_data_access +
        at48_bi_env_available + at49_it_architecture_asset +
        at50_central_data_env + at51_selfservice_dashboard +
        at52_advanced_analytics_tooling + at53_it_supports_operations +
        at54_cloud_datascience_use + at55_semantic_architecture

  # EM: Employee knowledge and skills
  EM =~ em56_data_stewardship + em57_standardized_workflow +
        em58_multidisciplinary_dashboards + em59_bi_analyst_available +
        em60_domain_it_link + em61_data_in_advice + em62_data_contact_point +
        em63_model_input_professional + em64_ops_algorithms_balance +
        em65_analytics_responsible_role + em66_tactical_algorithms_balance +
        em67_ai_input_professional

  # CO: Collaboration with others than own organisation
  CO =~ co68_digital_exchange_chain + co69_patient_secure_comm +
       co70_data_governance_partners + co71_interorg_data_meetings +
       co72_thematic_standardization + co73_digital_exchange_external +
       co74_pgo_collaboration + co75_interorg_data_analysis +
       co76_interorg_predictive_decisions + co77_population_health_data
'

fit_all  <- cfa(model, data = dat_all,  estimator = "WLSMV", ordered = names(dat_all))
fit_sens <- cfa(model, data = dat_sens, estimator = "WLSMV", ordered = names(dat_sens))

fm <- c("chisq.scaled", "df.scaled", "pvalue.scaled", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled")
cfa_table <- sapply(list(Primary = fit_all, Sensitivity = fit_sens),
                    function(f) round(as.numeric(fitMeasures(f, fm)), 3))
rownames(cfa_table) <- fm
print(cfa_table)

summary(fit_all, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
```

# 4. Exploratory factor analysis

The same function is applied to both samples: Spearman correlations, removal of
items that correlate below .20 with all other items, KMO and Bartlett, parallel
analysis, EFA (minres, oblimin), stepwise removal of items with all loadings
below the cut-off, and Cronbach's alpha.

```{r efa_function}
spearman_cor <- function(d) cor(d, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

run_efa <- function(dat, n_factors = 7, cutoff = 0.32, seed = 1) {
  out <- list(n = nrow(dat))

  # Step 1: correlation matrix; remove items with max |r| < .20, count pairs with |r| > .90
  R0 <- spearman_cor(dat)
  R0_off <- R0
  diag(R0_off) <- NA
  max_abs_r <- apply(abs(R0_off), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  out$weak_corr_items   <- names(max_abs_r)[max_abs_r < 0.2]
  out$n_high_corr_pairs <- sum(abs(R0_off) > 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) / 2
  d <- dat[, setdiff(names(dat), out$weak_corr_items), drop = FALSE]
  R <- spearman_cor(d)
  out$n_items_efa <- ncol(d)

  # Step 2: suitability
  out$kmo        <- psych::KMO(R)$MSA
  out$bartlett_p <- psych::cortest.bartlett(R, n = nrow(d))$p.value

  # Step 3: number of factors
  set.seed(seed)
  pa <- psych::fa.parallel(R, fm = "minres", fa = "fa", n.obs = nrow(d), plot = FALSE)
  out$ev_fa            <- pa$fa.values  # eigenvalues of the common-factor solution
  out$n_parallel       <- pa$nfact
  out$n_ev_fa_above_1  <- sum(pa$fa.values > 1)
  out$n_ev_cor_above_1 <- sum(eigen(R, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values > 1)  # Kaiser-Guttman

  # Step 4: EFA, then remove weakly loading items one at a time
  efa <- psych::fa(R, nfactors = n_factors, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres")
  out$var_initial      <- efa$Vaccounted
  out$loadings_initial <- unclass(efa$loadings)  # all loadings before item removal (Appendix 2)
  out$removed <- character(0)
  repeat {
    max_load <- apply(abs(unclass(efa$loadings)), 1, max)
    weak <- names(max_load)[max_load < cutoff]
    if (length(weak) == 0) break
    weakest <- weak[which.min(max_load[weak])]
    out$removed <- c(out$removed, weakest)
    d <- d[, setdiff(names(d), weakest), drop = FALSE]
    efa <- psych::fa(spearman_cor(d), nfactors = n_factors, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres")
  }

  # Step 5: final solution; each item is assigned to the factor with its highest loading
  L <- unclass(efa$loadings)
  out$efa <- efa
  out$loadings <- L
  out$var_final <- efa$Vaccounted
  out$factor_list <- split(rownames(L), colnames(L)[apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)])
  out$n_cross_loadings <- sum(apply(abs(L) >= cutoff, 1, sum) > 1)

  # Step 6: Cronbach's alpha per factor
  out$alpha <- sapply(out$factor_list, function(its) {
    if (length(its) < 2) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
      psych::alpha(d[, its, drop = FALSE], check.keys = TRUE)
    ))$total[["raw_alpha"]]
  })
  out
}

print_efa <- function(res) {
  cat("Items removed, max |r| < .20:", if (length(res$weak_corr_items) == 0) "none" else res$weak_corr_items, "\n")
  cat("Item pairs with |r| > .90:", res$n_high_corr_pairs, "\n")
  cat("KMO:", round(res$kmo, 2), "| Bartlett p:", format.pval(res$bartlett_p, digits = 3), "\n")
  cat("Parallel analysis:", res$n_parallel, "factors\n")
  cat("Common-factor eigenvalues > 1:", res$n_ev_fa_above_1, "\n")
  cat("Correlation-matrix eigenvalues > 1 (Kaiser-Guttman):", res$n_ev_cor_above_1, "\n")
  cat("\nVariance accounted for before item removal:\n")
  print(round(res$var_initial, 3))
  cat("\nItems removed, all |loadings| <", cutoff, "(", length(res$removed), "):\n")
  print(res$removed)
  cat("\nFinal solution:", nrow(res$loadings), "items. All loadings:\n")
  print(round(res$loadings[, sort(colnames(res$loadings))], 3))
  cat("\nVariance accounted for, final solution:\n")
  print(round(res$var_final, 3))
  cat("\nItems per factor and Cronbach's alpha:\n")
  print(rbind(n_items = lengths(res$factor_list), alpha = round(res$alpha, 3)))
  cat("\nInter-factor correlations (Phi):\n")
  print(round(res$efa$Phi, 3))
}

# Loading table in the layout of Multimedia Appendices 2 and 4:
# - all loadings are shown, factors in the order MR1, MR2, ..., MR7;
# - the first two rows are the sums of squared loadings and the explained variance (%)
#   from psych (Vaccounted, which takes the factor correlations into account);
# - items are grouped by the factor with their highest absolute loading and sorted from
#   high to low within each factor; items without any |loading| >= cutoff come last
#   (Factor = "none"), in questionnaire order.
appendix_table <- function(L, V, cutoff = 0.32) {
  f <- sort(colnames(L))
  L <- L[, f, drop = FALSE]
  V <- V[, f, drop = FALSE]
  main       <- apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)
  loads      <- apply(abs(L), 1, max) >= cutoff
  grp        <- ifelse(loads, f[main], "none")
  main_value <- L[cbind(seq_len(nrow(L)), main)]
  ord <- order(match(grp, c(f, "none")), ifelse(loads, -main_value, 0), seq_len(nrow(L)))

  items <- data.frame(Item    = toupper(substr(rownames(L), 1, 4)),
                      Content = sub("^[a-z]{2}[0-9]{2}_", "", rownames(L)),
                      Factor  = grp,
                      round(L, 3),
                      check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)[ord, ]
  header <- data.frame(Item    = c("SS loadings", "Explained variance (%)"),
                       Content = "", Factor = "",
                       rbind(round(V["SS loadings", ], 3), round(100 * V["Proportion Var", ], 1)),
                       check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  out <- rbind(header, items)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

# Shows an appendix table in the knitted document; loadings >= cutoff in bold
show_appendix <- function(tab, cutoff = 0.32) {
  mr  <- grep("^MR", names(tab))
  pct <- tab$Item == "Explained variance (%)"
  ss  <- tab$Item == "SS loadings"
  out <- tab
  for (j in mr) {
    x <- tab[[j]]
    s <- formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
    s[pct] <- formatC(x[pct], format = "f", digits = 1)
    bold <- !pct & !ss & abs(x) >= cutoff
    s[bold] <- paste0("**", s[bold], "**")
    out[[j]] <- s
  }
  knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", rep("r", length(mr))))
}
```

## 4.2 Sensitivity analysis (first assessment per organisation)

```{r efa_sensitivity}
res_sens <- run_efa(dat_sens, n_factors, cutoff, seed)
print_efa(res_sens)
```

# 5. Comparison of the primary and the sensitivity analysis

Factor solutions are compared with Tucker's congruence coefficient (.95 or
higher: factors can be considered equal; .85 to .94: fair similarity;
Lorenzo-Seva and ten Berge, 2006).

```{r comparison_functions}
# Tucker's congruence between the columns of two loading matrices
tucker <- function(A, B) crossprod(A, B) / sqrt(outer(colSums(A^2), colSums(B^2)))

# One-to-one matching of factors, starting with the highest |congruence|
match_factors <- function(phi) {
  P <- abs(phi)
  pairs <- NULL
  for (k in seq_len(min(dim(P)))) {
    idx <- which(P == max(P, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    pairs <- rbind(pairs, data.frame(reference = rownames(P)[idx[1]], comparison = colnames(P)[idx[2]],
                                     congruence = phi[idx[1], idx[2]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    P[idx[1], ] <- NA
    P[, idx[2]] <- NA
  }
  pairs[order(pairs$reference), ]
}
```

```{r comparison}
# Key results side by side
key_results <- function(res) c(
  "Assessments (n)"                                      = res$n,
  "Items removed, max |r| < .20"                         = length(res$weak_corr_items),
  "KMO overall MSA"                                      = round(res$kmo, 2),
  "Parallel analysis (factors)"                          = res$n_parallel,
  "Common-factor eigenvalues > 1"                        = res$n_ev_fa_above_1,
  "Correlation-matrix eigenvalues > 1 (Kaiser-Guttman)"  = res$n_ev_cor_above_1,
  "Cumulative variance before item removal (%)"          = round(100 * max(res$var_initial["Cumulative Var", ]), 1),
  "Items removed, all |loadings| < cut-off"              = length(res$removed),
  "Items in final solution"                              = nrow(res$loadings),
  "Cumulative variance final solution (%)"               = round(100 * max(res$var_final["Cumulative Var", ]), 1),
  "Items with cross-loadings"                            = res$n_cross_loadings,
  "Cronbach's alpha, lowest"                             = round(min(res$alpha, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  "Cronbach's alpha, highest"                            = round(max(res$alpha, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
)
comparison_table <- cbind(Primary = key_results(res_primary), Sensitivity = key_results(res_sens))
print(comparison_table)

# Comparison 1: same items. The seven-factor EFA is run in the sensitivity sample
# on exactly the items of the final primary solution.
L_primary <- res_primary$loadings
items_primary <- rownames(L_primary)
efa_same <- psych::fa(spearman_cor(dat_sens[, items_primary, drop = FALSE]),
                      nfactors = n_factors, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres")
L_same <- unclass(efa_same$loadings)[items_primary, , drop = FALSE]

cong_same <- match_factors(tucker(L_primary, L_same))
map <- setNames(cong_same$reference, cong_same$comparison)
same_factor <- unname(map[colnames(L_same)[apply(abs(L_same), 1, which.max)]]) ==
  colnames(L_primary)[apply(abs(L_primary), 1, which.max)]

cat("\nComparison 1 (same items): congruence of matched factors\n")
print(cong_same, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Items with their highest loading on the corresponding factor:", sum(same_factor), "of", length(same_factor), "\n")
cat("Items that move to another factor:", if (all(same_factor)) "none" else items_primary[!same_factor], "\n")

# Comparison 2: each analysis with its own item removal, compared on the items both retained
common_items <- intersect(items_primary, rownames(res_sens$loadings))
cong_own <- match_factors(tucker(L_primary[common_items, , drop = FALSE],
                                 res_sens$loadings[common_items, , drop = FALSE]))

cat("\nComparison 2 (own item removal): items retained in both analyses:", length(common_items), "\n")
print(cong_own, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Retained in the primary analysis only:", setdiff(items_primary, rownames(res_sens$loadings)), "\n")
cat("Retained in the sensitivity analysis only:", setdiff(rownames(res_sens$loadings), items_primary), "\n")
```

# 6. Six versus seven factors

The six-factor solution suggested by parallel analysis is compared with the
seven-factor solution: which factors combine, which items each solution
retains, and how the items are distributed over the factors.

```{r six_vs_seven_factors}
# Six-factor solution, same procedure as the seven-factor solution
res_6 <- run_efa(dat_all, n_factors = 6, cutoff, seed)
print_efa(res_6)

# Which factors of the seven-factor solution combine in the six-factor solution?
# Compared before item removal, on the same 76 items
d76 <- dat_all[, setdiff(names(dat_all), res_primary$weak_corr_items)]
efa7_init <- psych::fa(spearman_cor(d76), nfactors = 7, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres")
efa6_init <- psych::fa(spearman_cor(d76), nfactors = 6, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres")
# Check: the seven-factor fit here is the same as the one shown in Appendix 2
cat("Same fit as the one shown in Appendix 2:",
    isTRUE(all.equal(unclass(efa7_init$loadings), res_primary$loadings_initial)), "\n")
cat("\nCongruence before item removal (rows: 7 factors, columns: 6 factors):\n")
print(round(tucker(unclass(efa7_init$loadings), unclass(efa6_init$loadings)), 2))

# Final solutions, compared on the items both retained
common_67 <- intersect(rownames(res_primary$loadings), rownames(res_6$loadings))
cat("\nItems retained in both final solutions:", length(common_67), "\n")
cat("Congruence of the final solutions (rows: 7 factors, columns: 6 factors):\n")
print(round(tucker(res_primary$loadings[common_67, ], res_6$loadings[common_67, ]), 2))

# Item assignment side by side
assign7 <- setNames(colnames(res_primary$loadings)[apply(abs(res_primary$loadings), 1, which.max)],
                    rownames(res_primary$loadings))
assign6 <- setNames(colnames(res_6$loadings)[apply(abs(res_6$loadings), 1, which.max)],
                    rownames(res_6$loadings))
all_items <- union(names(assign7), names(assign6))
table_67 <- data.frame(item = all_items,
                       factor_7 = unname(assign7[all_items]),
                       factor_6 = unname(assign6[all_items]))
cat("\nCross-table of item assignment (NA = removed in that solution):\n")
print(table(factor_7 = table_67$factor_7, factor_6 = table_67$factor_6, useNA = "ifany"))
print(table_67[order(table_67$factor_7, table_67$factor_6), ], row.names = FALSE)
```
